dimensions.note: No credential is an argument and none is stored: the issued access token is never written, only its sub and roles claims. The Postgres (salmon/salmon), LDAP admin (admin/admin) and seeded user (password) credentials are fixed throwaway values of a local test stack, reachable only on the compose network; only Salmon's port is published. The push-time credentials-sensitive-field warnings on tokenDuration (a lifetime such as 10m) and tokenSubject (the token's sub claim) are the name heuristic, not secrets.
Every method logs at info on entry and completion with structured placeholders; nothing secret is logged (the token's sub and roles are identifiers, not credentials).

Commands throw with their argv and stderr; ensure throws with the tail of Salmon's logs when discovery does not answer in time; the fixture throws when the stack's Postgres is not running, when Salmon's schema never appears, or when there is no grant to revoke; token-exchange throws with Salmon's OAuth error. Every record is written after the work succeeded.

Unit tests cover the generated compose project, the LDAP seed, salmon.yaml, the issuer path rule, stable ids, SQL quoting and the seed transaction, the grant-names-an-app refinement and JWT claim decoding. The execute paths (docker and kubectl subprocesses) are not unit-tested with a mocked command; they were exercised live against a throwaway stack and kind cluster: ensure, seed, a token exchange returning roles [ldap/Registry-Push], revoke followed by an invalid_target refusal, reseeding replacing rows and resetting revoked flags, and stop leaving no containers. 2026.10.26.2 adds an assertion that the Postgres healthcheck uses TCP.

ensure is docker compose up -d (a no-op for a running, unchanged project) and stop is down (succeeds when the project is gone); seed replaces the fixture's rows in one transaction with ids derived from project, name and keys; revoking a grant that is already gone throws on purpose so a test notices a missing seed. 2026.10.26.2: the Postgres healthcheck runs pg_isready over TCP (-h 127.0.0.1); the socket check passed during the image's first-start init server, which listens on the Unix socket only, so Salmon could start, be refused over TCP and exit (seen in a pg-validator e2e run). Four consecutive fresh starts succeeded with the fix.
Discovery is accepted only on a 2xx; the token response must carry a string access_token, otherwise Salmon's error and error_description are reported; no list endpoints, so no pagination.
Subprocess output is read to the end and fetch bodies are cancelled; nothing is written to disk (the compose project goes on stdin); stop removes containers, network and volumes.

README examples use localhost and <cluster> placeholders; salmon.local is the LDAP domain of the seeded test directory, not infrastructure; the default image is the public registry.dataverket.org/tools/salmon the package exists to run.
All schemas are z.object without passthrough.
Every resource spec is lifetime infinite with garbageCollection 10 (stack, fixture) or 20 (token-exchange result).
Test fixtures, not managed resources: stack has ensure and stop, fixture has seed (create-or-replace) and revoke, token-exchange has test; update and sync have no meaning for a throwaway stack.
The mutating methods act on a local throwaway compose project and its database, which the definitions name; there is no shared or remote resource to guard.
Each method writes one instance of one spec (stack, fixture, result).
No method reads back stored state; the fixture reads the live database for which grants exist.

Only the package version moves to 2026.10.26.2; the model types and their schemas are unchanged, so no upgrade entry is needed. 2026.10.27.1 relicenses the extension to AGPL-3.0-only (LICENSE.md, manifest license, README); no code change.
